performed_via_github_app.description:
# Transforming Code Reviews with AI

## Features

**Automated Reviews**: Continuous reviews of the pull requests including incremental commits. 

**Summarization**: Generates high-level summary and a technical walkthrough of the PR changes. 

**Line-by-line review**: Provides line-by-line suggestions committable with one click.

**Codebase verification**:  Verifies the impact on the overall codebase and identifies missing changes.

**Insights into your code**:  Ask any questions on your codebase within the pull request 

**Chat about your code** : Chat with the bot around your code. The more you chat, the smarter it gets.

**Issue Validation**:  Validates the PR against the linked issues and identifies other related issues

Code Review by Qodo

🐞 Bugs (1) 📘 Rule violations (0) 📜 Skill insights (0)
1. Legacy subclasses fail dispatch 🐞 Bug ≡ Correctness
>
>Description >
> >
>Removing the subclass adapters makes Flask 3.1-style overrides such as dispatch_request(self)
>receive an unexpected AppContext, causing request dispatch or teardown to fail with TypeError.
>The deleted warning explicitly promised support until Flask 4.0, while this branch is the unreleased
>3.2 release.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[src/flask/app.py[L308-309]](https://github.com/seonho12-54/qodo-coderabbit-benchmark/pull/6240/files#diff-d3e0349504081bb501c611b3954be364188a4cf442056181272e27e830ae446eL308-L309) > >```diff >- setattr(cls, method.__name__, remove_ctx(method)) >- setattr(Flask, method.__name__, add_ctx(base_method)) >``` >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>The WSGI entry point passes ctx to full_dispatch_request and handle_exception; those methods
>then pass it to overridable dispatch, preprocessing, finalization, logging, and response hooks. With
>the deleted adapters, any existing override that accepts only the previously public arguments
>receives one extra positional argument; the changelog identifies this branch as unreleased Flask 3.2
>rather than the Flask 4.0 removal boundary named by the deleted deprecation warning.
>
> > [src/flask/app.py[1508-1516]](https://github.com/seonho12-54/qodo-coderabbit-benchmark/blob/2ac81868274b34c9a4a2788d07ead14cc093e970/src/flask/app.py/#L1508-L1516) > [src/flask/app.py[908-935]](https://github.com/seonho12-54/qodo-coderabbit-benchmark/blob/2ac81868274b34c9a4a2788d07ead14cc093e970/src/flask/app.py/#L908-L935) > [src/flask/app.py[813-864]](https://github.com/seonho12-54/qodo-coderabbit-benchmark/blob/2ac81868274b34c9a4a2788d07ead14cc093e970/src/flask/app.py/#L813-L864) > [src/flask/app.py[1282-1334]](https://github.com/seonho12-54/qodo-coderabbit-benchmark/blob/2ac81868274b34c9a4a2788d07ead14cc093e970/src/flask/app.py/#L1282-L1334) > [src/flask/app.py[1336-1395]](https://github.com/seonho12-54/qodo-coderabbit-benchmark/blob/2ac81868274b34c9a4a2788d07ead14cc093e970/src/flask/app.py/#L1336-L1395) > [CHANGES.rst[1-4]](https://github.com/seonho12-54/qodo-coderabbit-benchmark/blob/2ac81868274b34c9a4a2788d07ead14cc093e970/CHANGES.rst/#L1-L4) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >Removing `Flask.__init_subclass__` and its argument adapters breaks subclasses overriding lifecycle methods with their Flask 3.1 signatures. Internal dispatch now passes an `AppContext` unconditionally, so these overrides raise `TypeError` despite the compatibility period previously extending through Flask 3.x. > >## Issue Context >Restore compatibility without globally mutating methods on `Flask`, or retain the released method signatures and obtain the active context internally. Add regression tests covering old-signature dispatch, error handling, response processing, and teardown overrides, including overrides that call `super()`. > >## Fix Focus Areas >- src/flask/app.py[79-79] >- src/flask/app.py[882-935] >- src/flask/app.py[1282-1370] >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >
Context sources
Review mode: ⚖️ Balanced: This removes compatibility machinery for subclass method signatures in Flask’s central dispatch path, creating meaningful public-behavior and backward-compatibility risk despite being localized to one file.

### The AI Code Review Platform

## Get Started
Simply sign into Github and click the "Configure" button. Check out our documentation for more info: https://docs.qodo.ai/get-started.

## Overview
Qodo automatically reviews every GitHub pull request, identifies logic bugs, edge cases, security issues, and code quality problems, and provides actionable suggestions your team can apply immediately.

Install in minutes. Integrates seamlessly into your existing workflows.

## Qodo is designed for developers who:
- Handle frequent pull requests and need reliable review coverage
- Balance code quality with fast delivery
- Work in complex, multi-repo systems
- Use AI-generated code and need stronger guardrails
- Build production software where reliability matters

## Qodo Capabilities
- ## Automated PR Analysis
  - Reviews every pull request automatically
  - No manual trigger required

- ## Context-Aware Code Review
  - Understands cross-file changes
  - Detects architectural inconsistencies

- ## Actionable Suggestions
  - Concrete code fixes
  - Clear explanations
  - Prioritized feedback

- ## Security & Reliability Checks
  - Identifies risky patterns
  - Reduces attack surface area
